nodes.name: Bands 1–3: The Reactive Range
nodes.description: Bands 1–3 are the reactive range: identity is fused with thought and role, and practice works by interrupting automatic reaction rather than by producing stillness.

nodes.name: Bands 4–6: The Inward Range

nodes.name: Body Scan for Anxiety
nodes.description: A slow, wide body scan lowers anxiety by widening attention beyond the chest and head, where anxious attention usually concentrates.

nodes.name: The Boredom Spike
nodes.description: Boredom in practice is a sharp, time-limited rise in aversion that peaks early and fades if not acted on, which is why the first minutes feel harder than the last.

nodes.name: Box Breathing
nodes.description: Equal-count inhale, hold, exhale and hold create a stable, low-variability breath rhythm that supports sustained attention without drowsiness.

nodes.name: 4-7-8 Breathing
nodes.description: 4-7-8 breathing pairs a short inhale with a long exhale and a brief hold, producing a reliable downshift in arousal within a few cycles.

nodes.name: The "Gut Feeling Is Always Right" Myth
nodes.description: A gut feeling is a fast prediction built from past experience, so it is only as reliable as the experience it was trained on.

nodes.name: Heart Rate Variability
nodes.description: Heart rate variability is the variation in time between heartbeats; higher resting variability generally tracks better autonomic flexibility and faster recovery.

nodes.name: Effort Headache in Practice
nodes.description: Head and jaw pain during practice usually comes from sustained muscular effort in the face, neck and eyes while trying to concentrate.

nodes.name: Sleep Efficiency
nodes.description: Sleep efficiency is time asleep divided by time in bed; it separates a sleep problem from a schedule problem.

nodes.name: The Witness Gap
nodes.description: The witness gap is the interval between a stimulus and a reaction; practice widens it until the reaction becomes optional.

passages.heading: Definition
passages.text: Boredom in practice is a sharp, time-limited rise in aversion that peaks early and fades if not acted on, which is why the first minutes feel harder than the last.

passages.heading: Mechanism
passages.text: 1. Novelty drops when the object of attention stays the same. 2. Aversion rises as the predicted reward falls. 3. The mind proposes alternatives with higher predicted reward. 4. Acting on an alternative ends the spike and teaches avoidance. 5. Not acting lets the spike decay on its own.

passages.heading: Why it happens
passages.text: Prediction systems are tuned to rate of change. A stable object reads as "nothing new", which is misread as "nothing valuable".

passages.heading: Signs
passages.text:
• Strong urge to check progress at minute three
• Mental list-making during practice
• Feeling that time has slowed
• Sudden craving for music, food or news

passages.heading: What it is not
passages.text: Boredom is not evidence that the object is unimportant. It is evidence that the prediction system has stopped updating.

passages.heading: Practice: Detail widening (During each spike, 60 seconds)
passages.text: Find three new details in the same object: temperature, texture, beginning, ending. Novelty is restored by resolution, not by switching.

passages.heading: How to measure
passages.text: Minute at which the spike peaks and whether the sit continues past it.

passages.heading: Definition
passages.text: Head and jaw pain during practice usually comes from sustained muscular effort in the face, neck and eyes while trying to concentrate.

passages.heading: Mechanism
passages.text: 1. Concentration is attempted with a held brow and fixed gaze. 2. Neck and jaw muscles co-contract without awareness. 3. Sustained contraction reduces local blood flow and produces ache. 4. The ache is read as a sign of deep practice. 5. The pattern is repeated and becomes the default posture.

passages.heading: Why it happens
passages.text: The body follows the instruction literally: "focus" recruits the muscles that visually aim, even when the eyes are closed.

passages.heading: Signs
passages.text:
• Ache behind the eyes or at the temples
• Jaw soreness after sitting
• Relief when the eyes soften or the tongue relaxes
• Headache that appears only on practice days

passages.heading: What it is not
passages.text: This is not spiritual opening, detox or energy movement. It is ordinary muscular load with a story attached.

passages.heading: Practice: Soft-face reset (Every 2 minutes during practice)
passages.text: Soften the tongue from the palate, unclench the jaw, widen the peripheral gaze, drop the shoulders. Then return to the object.

passages.heading: How to measure
passages.text: Headache rating before and after practice across a week.

passages.heading: Caution
passages.text: New or severe headaches, especially with vision change, need medical assessment.

passages.heading: Definition
passages.text: 4-7-8 breathing pairs a short inhale with a long exhale and a brief hold, producing a reliable downshift in arousal within a few cycles.

passages.heading: Mechanism
passages.text: 1. Extended exhale increases vagal braking on the heart. 2. The hold after exhale briefly reduces CO2 drive and slows the next inhale. 3. Heart rate falls and attention narrows to the breath. 4. Arousal drops enough for sleep onset or for settling before practice.

passages.heading: Why it happens
passages.text: Breath is the fastest voluntary lever on autonomic state; exhale-dominant patterns favour parasympathetic activity.

passages.heading: Signs
passages.text:
• Shoulders drop without being told to
• Mental pace slows after four cycles
• Sleepiness within two minutes when lying down
• Reduced urge to move

passages.heading: What it is not
passages.text: This is not hyperventilation and not deep breathing. Volume stays normal; only the timing changes.

passages.heading: Practice: Four-cycle settle (4 cycles, twice daily, or before sleep)
passages.text: Inhale 4, hold 7, exhale 8, no pause after exhale. Stop at any dizziness and breathe normally.

passages.heading: How to measure
passages.text: Time to settle (minutes) and resting pulse before and after.

passages.heading: Caution
passages.text: Skip breath holds during pregnancy, with uncontrolled blood pressure, or if holds cause dizziness.

passages.heading: Definition
passages.text: Equal-count inhale, hold, exhale and hold create a stable, low-variability breath rhythm that supports sustained attention without drowsiness.

passages.heading: Mechanism
passages.text: 1. Equal segment lengths reduce breath-to-breath variability. 2. Predictable rhythm lowers vigilance load. 3. Moderate CO2 retention stabilises attention without sedation. 4. The counting task occupies working memory lightly. 5. A stable state supports longer sits.

passages.heading: Why it happens
passages.text: Attention is easier to hold on a predictable signal than on an unpredictable one; the rhythm itself becomes the anchor.

passages.heading: Signs
passages.text:
• Steadier posture after two minutes
• Counting that continues without effort
• Less drowsiness than with long exhales
• Breath that feels mechanical rather than emotional

passages.heading: What it is not
passages.text: Box breathing is not a relaxation exercise by design. Its main effect is attentional stability; calm is a side effect.

passages.heading: Practice: Four-square (3–5 minutes before practice)
passages.text: Inhale 4, hold 4, exhale 4, hold 4. Keep the counts equal and the breath quiet.

passages.heading: How to measure
passages.text: Sit length completed and subjective steadiness rating.

passages.heading: Definition
passages.text: A slow, wide body scan lowers anxiety by widening attention beyond the chest and head, where anxious attention usually concentrates.

passages.heading: Mechanism
passages.text: 1. Anxiety narrows attention to threat-relevant regions. 2. A sequential scan forces attention into neutral areas. 3. Interoceptive resolution increases and prediction error falls. 4. Threat appraisal drops as the body map becomes less alarming. 5. Widened attention is easier to maintain than suppressed thought.

passages.heading: Why it happens
passages.text: Anxiety is partly a spatial habit of attention. Moving attention changes the input that the appraisal system is working from.

passages.heading: Signs
passages.text:
• Chest tightness easing when attention reaches the legs
• Breath slowing without deliberate control
• Less mental commentary as the scan proceeds
• Sleepiness rather than alertness at the end

passages.heading: What it is not
passages.text: This is not relaxation training. The scan can surface discomfort; the instruction is to report, not to remove.

passages.heading: Practice: Wide scan (12 minutes, once daily)
passages.text: Move from feet to head in ten regions, two breaths per region. Name quality and intensity, never analyse the cause.

passages.heading: How to measure
passages.text: Anxiety rating (0–10) before and after, plus number of regions felt clearly.

passages.heading: Caution
passages.text: If scanning reliably increases distress, shorten it and work with a trauma-informed guide.

passages.heading: Definition
passages.text: The witness gap is the interval between a stimulus and a reaction; practice widens it until the reaction becomes optional.

passages.heading: Mechanism
passages.text: 1. A trigger produces an automatic appraisal. 2. Without training, appraisal and response are fused. 3. Repeated noticing inserts a pause between them. 4. The pause allows a second appraisal. 5. Choice becomes possible inside the pause.

passages.heading: Why it happens
passages.text: Awareness does not stop the reaction; it delays it long enough for a different response to be selected.

passages.heading: Signs
passages.text:
• Hearing yourself before speaking
• Noticing anger as heat before it becomes a sentence
• A half-second of choice where there used to be none
• Regret after reactions becoming less frequent

passages.heading: What it is not
passages.text: The gap is not detachment or numbness. It is not the absence of emotion; it is the presence of a choice inside emotion.

passages.heading: Practice: One-second pause (Every trigger, for 21 days)
passages.text: On noticing a reaction, exhale once before responding. Name the state silently. Then choose.

passages.heading: How to measure
passages.text: Reactions you would have regretted per week.

passages.heading: Definition
passages.text: Heart rate variability is the variation in time between heartbeats; higher resting variability generally tracks better autonomic flexibility and faster recovery.

passages.heading: Mechanism
passages.text: 1. Beat-to-beat intervals change with breath and autonomic traffic. 2. Higher variability at rest reflects stronger vagal modulation. 3. Acute stress and illness typically lower variability. 4. Recovery is visible as variability returning to a personal baseline. 5. Trends matter more than any single reading.

passages.heading: Why it happens
passages.text: A flexible heart responds to continuous demand. A rigid rhythm suggests the system is holding one state.

passages.heading: Signs
passages.text:
• Morning readings that swing with sleep and alcohol
• Lower values on high-load days
• Recovery visible over 2–3 days after stress
• Breath-paced readings higher than spontaneous ones

passages.heading: What it is not
passages.text: Higher is not always better. Very high values can reflect arrhythmia or measurement artefact; this is why trends and context matter.

passages.heading: Practice: Standardised morning reading (60 seconds, same time daily)
passages.text: Measure before standing, before caffeine, three days a week minimum. Record sleep hours beside it.

passages.heading: How to measure
passages.text: Seven-day rolling average compared with your own 30-day baseline.

passages.heading: Caution
passages.text: Wearable HRV is not a diagnostic measure. Persistent abnormalities need clinical review.

passages.heading: Definition
passages.text: Sleep efficiency is time asleep divided by time in bed; it separates a sleep problem from a schedule problem.

passages.heading: Mechanism
passages.text: 1. Time in bed is recorded from lights out to rising. 2. Time asleep is recorded from estimates or a tracker. 3. The ratio exposes wake time spent in bed. 4. Low ratios usually reflect a stretched window rather than a sleep defect. 5. Compressing the window often restores the ratio.

passages.heading: Why it happens
passages.text: The brain associates the bed with wakefulness when wake time in bed is long. Association, not willpower, governs sleep onset.

passages.heading: Signs
passages.text:
• More than 30 minutes awake before sleep most nights
• Long lie-ins that do not improve freshness
• Falling asleep quickly away from your own bed
• Weekend sleep far longer than weekday sleep

passages.heading: What it is not
passages.text: High efficiency with short sleep is not healthy sleep. The ratio must be read with total duration.

passages.heading: Practice: Fixed window (Same 7.5-hour window for 14 nights)
passages.text: Set wake time first, then bedtime. Leave the bed after 20 awake minutes and return when sleepy.

passages.heading: How to measure
passages.text: Weekly efficiency percentage alongside average duration.

passages.heading: Definition
passages.text: Bands 1–3 are the reactive range: identity is fused with thought and role, and practice works by interrupting automatic reaction rather than by producing stillness.

passages.heading: Mechanism
passages.text: 1. Identity is built from roles, opinions and comparison. 2. Threat is experienced as loss of role or approval. 3. Attention is almost entirely outward-facing. 4. Stillness is interpreted as boredom or danger. 5. Short, frequent interruptions of reaction land better than long sits.

passages.heading: Why it happens
passages.text: At this band the nervous system is solving for safety and status. Practices that ask for sustained inward attention outrun the available capacity.

passages.heading: Signs
passages.text:
• Practice feels pointless without a visible benefit
• Strong investment in being right
• Mood tied to external response
• Long sits produce restlessness rather than insight

passages.heading: What it is not
passages.text: This is not a deficiency. It is a stage with its own valid methods; the error is applying band-6 practices at band 2.

passages.heading: Practice: Two-minute reaction log (Twice daily, 2 minutes)
passages.text: Write one reaction, the trigger, and what it protected. No analysis beyond one line each.

passages.heading: How to measure
passages.text: Number of reactions caught before acting, per week.

passages.heading: Definition
passages.text: Bands 4–6 are the inward range: attention can be sustained, identity loosens from role, and practice shifts from interrupting reactions to investigating the observer.

passages.heading: Mechanism
passages.text: 1. Sustained attention becomes available for the first time. 2. Identity begins to be questioned rather than defended. 3. The witness is noticed intermittently. 4. Stillness becomes tolerable and then interesting. 5. The main risk shifts from restlessness to spiritual bypassing.

passages.heading: Why it happens
passages.text: Capacity has caught up with instruction. The obstacle is no longer restlessness; it is the subtle use of insight to avoid feeling.

passages.heading: Signs
passages.text:
• Longer sits complete without effort
• Genuine curiosity about the observer
• Language of detachment appearing in daily life
• Discomfort avoided through "witnessing" it

passages.heading: What it is not
passages.text: Equanimity is not indifference. If the witness stance protects you from grief, it is bypassing, not witnessing.

passages.heading: Practice: Inquiry after stillness (10 minutes sitting + 3 written lines)
passages.text: Ask "who is aware of this?" after the sit, then write what remains when the question is dropped.

passages.heading: How to measure
passages.text: Ratio of felt emotion to reported emotion in the weekly journal.

passages.heading: Caution
passages.text: Spiritual bypassing at this range can delay needed psychological work.

passages.heading: Definition
passages.text: A gut feeling is a fast prediction built from past experience, so it is only as reliable as the experience it was trained on.

passages.heading: Mechanism
passages.text: 1. The body signals a prediction before conscious reasoning completes. 2. The signal is based on learned associations, not on current evidence. 3. Confidence in the signal rises with emotional intensity. 4. Intensity is mistaken for accuracy. 5. The prediction is read as information rather than as a hypothesis.

passages.heading: Why it happens
passages.text: Fast prediction is cheap and usually good enough. It does not carry a label that distinguishes trained intuition from old fear.

passages.heading: Signs
passages.text:
• Certainty that arrives before any evidence
• Gut warnings that repeat across unrelated situations
• Strong conviction that resists contrary facts
• Physical signal that changes when you slow down

passages.heading: What it is not
passages.text: This is not an argument for ignoring the body. The signal is data; it is not a verdict.

passages.heading: Practice: Prediction check (One gut call per day, for 14 days)
passages.text: Write the prediction and the evidence it rests on, then record the outcome. Review the hit rate weekly.

passages.heading: How to measure
passages.text: Prediction accuracy over 14 days, split by domain.

passages.heading: 1. The app, plainly

Satyug (product name HOPE, internal name ConsciousOS) is a consciousness-development
platform that behaves like a companion rather than a content library. It is built on
one proprietary spine:

- 11 spiral bands (0–10, Survival → Source) computed from behavior, not self-report
 (firstElevenEngine.ts:31–43).
- 650 named loops of conditioning, each with triggers, manifestations, awareness
 markers, and a dissolution path (src/data/loops.ts:88–885, 28 categories).

 (firstElevenTypes.ts:12).

 (src/lib/sutra/practices.ts:5–33).

 (src/lib/session/types.ts:14–23).

The app's philosophy is designed for obsolescence: it is meant to become unnecessary.
That philosophy is why the eleven sittings matter more than they look — they are the

passages.heading: 3. The First Eleven today — honest mechanics audit
passages.text:
What already works (keep):

| Mechanic | Where | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Closed authored spine per sitting | firstElevenSessions.ts:15–450 | teaching → open → deepen → silence/breath → body → mirror → choice → act |
| Adaptive question fill | firstElevenEngine.ts:94–161 | deterministic scoring: weakest dimension +3, active loop +2, in-sitting variety −2, per-user hash tiebreak |
| 110-question bank | firstElevenQuestions.ts | choice / scale / text kinds; every option carries band + dimension + loop ids |
| Carry-seed rosary | firstElevenSessions.ts + useFirstEleven | one line out per sitting, quoted at the next threshold |
| The Dock — chat as a property of every step | TheDock.tsx + useSittingDock.ts | guide-chat edge, seeded with sitting, master, step, and every word typed; kept lines sharpen the mapping |
| Threshold / close / complete phases | FirstElevenScreen.tsx:144–307 | last carry-seed shown as "Left with last time" |
| Mapping analyzer | firstElevenEngine.ts:179–244 | weighted band (Light Six 0.6, Foundation 1.0, sittings weighted 1 + n/11) |
| 8 ranked journeys | journeyDefinitions.ts:27–129 | explainable scoring, every point carries its reason |
| Progress persistence + publish | useFirstEleven.ts, usePublishMirror.ts | local-first, resumes mid-run |

What is missing (the gap this blueprint closes):

1. No teacher presence in the sitting itself. The teaching step is a wall of
 prose with one attributed quote. Nobody is talking to you. The Dock exists but is
 a generic assistant — it is not the sitting's master, and it never speaks first.
2. No practice layer. Sitting 3 has a breath pattern and sitting 1 has a silence
 timer, but they are static timers. The app ships 232 conscious games with
 verified signal capture — none of them is reachable from the eleven sittings.
3. No mid-sitting adaptation. The spine is fixed once. If sitting 9 cracks
 someone open at minute two, nothing notices. The session engines already support
 morphs; the eleven do not use them.
4. No voice. The masters have ElevenLabs voices and pre-warmed caches
 (tts-speak, ttsPrewarm.ts) — the teaching steps are silent text.
5. No vow ledger. Each sitting ends in a vow ("I'll take one hour back") that
 is never recalled. Sitting 2 never asks whether sitting 1's vow was kept.
6. No cross-threading. Loops detected in the games, journal, and guide never
 re-enter the sittings. The 650-loop library is read by the engines; the eleven
 only see the 84-loop curated slice via the question options.
7. The mapping is a one-shot reveal. It is computed at the end and rendered
 once. It never updates, never surprises, never says "this sharpened."

passages.heading: 7. The detection stack

| Engine | What it reads | What it writes |

| live-detect | real-time in-session signals | loop activations, state shifts |
| signal-fusion | merges all signal sources into one state assessment | unified state → consciousness engine |
| pattern-window | long-horizon recurrence | recurring patterns invisible in real time |

passages.heading: 14. The v2 global spine
passages.text:
Every sitting keeps its authored bones and gains five layers. The spine becomes:

 

The seven upgrades (global):

1. The master speaks first. The opening line of every sitting is delivered in
 the sitting master's voice (ElevenLabs, pre-warmed), and it quotes one thing the
 user actually said — last sitting's carry-seed, last sitting's final answer, or
 the loudest loop so far. Not "tell me about your day." The name of the feeling,
 gifted back as a question.
2. A practice layer from the 232. Each sitting gains a game/breath/silence
 practice matched to its faculty, with mic verification where the game supports
 it. Its signals write to the same consciousnesssignals schema and feed the
 mapping. Sixty seconds of real measurement inside a six-minute sitting.
3. The conversational grammar in The Dock. The Dock already exists; it now
 speaks in the bounded ritual from the v4 session blueprint — OPEN the loop,
 WAIT (≤60s, empty UI, the orb stills), MIRROR the exact fragment, DEEPEN once
 (branched on reply type), CLOSE with a seed. One deepen per step, ever. Silence
 is a first-class answer: "You didn't answer. That's an answer too."
4. Mid-sitting morph, visible. Telemetry (answer latency, skips, dock sentiment,
 breath coherence) runs a tier:fast check at two points per sitting:
 keep | insertbreath | shorten | swapfocus. Max 2 morphs per sitting; distress
 sentiment forces soft morphs only; adaptation is announced — two skips draw the
 line "The night shortens."
5. The vow ledger. Every sitting's vow is stored and recalled at the next
 sitting's threshold — "Last time you said: I'll take one hour back. Did the hour
 happen?" No guilt either way; the answer itself is a band signal (integrity →
 karma faculty).
6. Kept lines become the rosary. Dock kept-lines already sharpen the mapping;
 they now also return at the close of each sitting and at the next threshold,
 alongside the carry-seed. The user's best sentences become the app's memory of them.
7. The mapping sharpens in public. After every sitting, one line changes on a
 visible "the map" card — band coordinate, strongest/weakest dimension, loudest
 loop. The mapping stops being a receipt and becomes a living reading.

Safety rules carried over: sitting 9 (death) and sitting 10 (numbing) force soft
morphs only, longer silence caps, and the option to stop early with the sitting
credited. Dark-night protocol hooks stay armed.

---

passages.heading: 15. Sitting 1 — The Stolen Mind
passages.text:
Attention is the last private property. Check who holds the deed. — Krishnamurti

Keep: the teaching (it is the best first minute in the product), the open
question pair, the silence, the one-hour vow.

Change:
- Opening (voiced, Krishnamurti): names the behavior before the theory —

 estimate from the Light Six conditioning seed.
- Practice layer: bell-in-the-wind (public, playable — tab-blur and

- Loop watch: BHV007 (automatic reach), AVD001, HAB001, CTL003,

- Morph: if tab-blur events during the practice exceed threshold, the sitting

- More-thread: the full attention ladder waits in the Temple — Dharana,

passages.heading: 16. Sitting 2 — The Comparison Machine

- Practice layer: comparison-scroll — a controlled feed that measures the

- Morph: heavy sentiment → drop the deepen question, extend silence to 75s.

passages.heading: 17. Sitting 3 — Desire and the More

passages.heading: 18. Sitting 4 — The Fear Engine

Change:

passages.heading: 20. Sitting 6 — The Mirror of Others

Every relationship is a mirror — most of us only see our own face in it. — Rumi

Keep: the unspoken-request teaching; the one-honest-sentence act.

Change:

passages.heading: 21. Sitting 7 — Money and Enough

Scarcity is a state of the nervous system, not a number in an account. — Krishna

Change:
- Opening: band-aware. If the mapping's band is 0–2, the sitting opens with

passages.heading: 22. Sitting 8 — Work and Worth

If your output stopped, who would you be? Sit with that question. — Vivekananda

Keep: the invisible-ledger teaching; the unearned-rest act.

Change:
- Opening: uses the vow ledger (rest was likely the hardest vow so far) and the

- Loop watch: PRD001, VAL008, MOT011, BHV007.
- Morph: if answers turn fast and frictionless (possible performance mode),

passages.heading: 23. Sitting 9 — Time and Death
passages.text:
You will die. That is not morbid — it is the only fact that makes urgency honest. — Buddha

Keep: everything. This is the heaviest sitting and the spine is right.

Change:
- Opening: a bell, then silence, then one sentence — "This is the heaviest

- More-thread: Bardo Room — the liminal faculty — for when the mind wants to

passages.heading: 24. Sitting 10 — The Conditioned Heart
passages.text:
Numbness is not peace. It is a feeling that learned it was unsafe. — Meera

Keep: the feeling-that-went-underground teaching; the name-one-feeling act.

Change:
- Opening (Meera, voiced): devotional register, no psychology — "I have gone

- Practice layer: grief-wave (if the sitting-9 flag is set, the grief is

- Morph: numbed-flat answers (scale pinned to the minimum, latency near zero)

- Vow: name one feeling precisely. Ledger asks at sitting 11.
- More-thread: Read the Emotional Weather — Meera — and the Forgiveness

passages.heading: 25. Sitting 11 — Who Is Asking?

All ten sittings asked about you. This one asks who 'you' is. — Ramana Maharshi

Keep: the turn; the three-round silence; the once-a-day return.

Change:
- Opening: the only opening that quotes nothing external — a bell, and

4. The Day-7 Return (new): seven days after sitting 11, the app offers one

passages.heading: 27. Ideas worth building
passages.text:
1. The two-minute sitting. Every sitting gets a compressed variant (breath +
 one question + vow) for the day the user has two minutes. The eleven become a
 daily practice, not a one-time gate — the closed spine makes this trivial to
 author.
2. Voice-first mode. Teachings delivered in the master's voice with subtitle;
 answers by speech (Deepgram STT is wired). Sittings 9 and 10 become listenable
 with eyes closed.
3. Band-branched teachings beyond sitting 7. The same authored teaching, three
 registers (survival / becoming / witness). One file edit per sitting; the
 composer already thinks in levels.
4. Loop christening. When a loop is confirmed across three sittings, the app
 gives it a name from the 650-library and the user meets it as a character with
 a history — never as a diagnosis. Loop-threading as depth, not repetition:
 fire 1 name it, fire 3 what it protects, fire 6 what it costs others, fire 9
 "who would you be without it?"
5. Kept-lines talisman. The close of sitting 11 mints a card of the user's best
 kept lines — shareable, printable, the app's only souvenir.
6. Master-of-the-sitting choice. After sitting 3, the user may swap any
 sitting's master for another from the roster with the same faculty. The voice
 changes; the spine does not.
7. The Eleven, walked together (enterprise). A cohort version where colleagues
 walk the sittings on the same week with private mirrors and a facilitator
 dashboard — the n≥5 aggregator pattern already exists.
8. Language parity. The 110-question bank and 11 teachings translate through
 the 40+ locale system; the carry-seeds are short enough to be hand-checked in
 every language. This is the cheapest global unlock in the product.
9. Signal honesty panel. One screen, visible to the user: what the app
 measured during the eleven (latency, skips, breath, kept lines) and what it
 inferred. Memory the user can audit is memory that earns trust.
10. The 12th sitting that does not exist. Do not author a twelfth. Instead,
 the Day-7 Return (above) and the journey doors are the twelfth. Restraint is
 the brand.

passages.heading: 28. Build order (by leverage per week)
passages.text:
1. Week of wiring, almost no backend: the master speaks first (TTS on the
 opening line, quoting the last carry-seed); the vow ledger at every threshold;
 "the map sharpens" card after each sitting; the two-minute variants. All four
 touch existing components only.
2. The practice layer: wire sittings 1, 3, 4, 9 to the games that already
 exist (bell-in-the-wind, craving-wave, fear-ladder, maranasati), with
 signals writing to the mapping. One integration, eleven sittings deepen.
3. The Dock ritual: OPEN/WAIT/MIRROR/DEEPEN/CLOSE grammar, one deepen per
 step, silence as an answer. Kept lines to the rosary.
4. Morphs + safety: telemetry capture, two check points, visible copy, soft-only
 rules for sittings 9–10, dark-night flag.
5. Band-branched teachings (sitting 7 first), voice-first mode, language parity.
6. The Day-7 Return and the talisman card — the close of the loop.
